In this project, I will be taking a look at plastic collection data from [*Break Free From Plastic*](https://www.breakfreefromplastic.org/)'s cleanups in 2019 and 2020. Specifically, I would like to understand the distribution of plastic they collected from select companies such as Nestlé, PepsiCo, and Coca-Cola.

![](https://www.breakfreefromplastic.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Brand-Audit-2022-Jibriel-Firman-03116-Annisa-Dian-Ndari-min.jpg){height=4in}
![](https://www.breakfreefromplastic.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/garbage-patch-coca-cola-is-this-yours-diver.jpg){height=4in}

Above left: Image of plastic cleanup from a [*Break Free From Plastic*](https://www.breakfreefromplastic.org/) cleanup event.

Above right: Image of a diver holding a coke bottle and a sign saying "Coca-cola is this yours?"

---

### Libraries

Load the libraries:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)          # For many things including ggplot and dplyr
library(here)               # For easy saving and deploying
library(mapdata)            # For maps
library(rsconnect)          # For deploying
```


Load in the data: 

```{r}

# bring csv information into R
plastics <- read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2021/2021-01-26/plastics.csv')

```


Let's see what this data looks like:

```{r}

# look at the first 4 rows
head(plastics, n = 4)

```


With the plastic data, we could do several things. We could explore the number of events per country in a heatmap. We could also make a heatmap of the number of participants, or amount of plastic per country. In this case, I am curious about what countries specific companies' plastics end up.

---

### Mapping:

Load in the base world map:

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| label: fig-basemap
#| fig-cap: "Basic world map."

# pull world map data
world <- map_data("world")


# plot the base world map to see what it looks like:
ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = world,
               aes(x = long, 
                   y = lat,
                   group = group),
               color = "darkgray",
               fill = "lightgray")+
  guides(fill = "none")

```


---

### Identify companies of interest:

Nestlé, PepsiCo, and The Coca-Cola Company all use plastics extensively in their packaging.

![](https://1000logos.net/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/Nestle-Logo-2015.png){width=2in}
![](https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/cdn.designcrowd.com/blog/The-Pepsi-Logo-History/Pepsi-Logo.jpg){width=2in}
![](https://1000logos.net/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Coca-Cola-logo.png){width=2in}


###### All logos above are copyright to their respective owners.

Let's take a closer look at where and how many of their plastics were found during cleanup events.

---

### Join datasets:

First we must full_join the world map and plastics datasets. Where do they match up? The column named region/country. The headings are different. Let's fix that.

```{r}

plastics |> 
  
  # first, rename the region column in plastics to match the country column in world
  rename(region = country) |> 
  
  #then, inner_join
  full_join(world) -> world_plastics

```

OK, that dataset seems a bit massive with 12,467,737 rows. Let's see how it looks for the first few rows to make sure the join worked ok.

```{r}

# print the first few rows
head(world_plastics)

```


Let's extract our companies of interest so we aren't wrangling 12 million rows. Let's try Coca-Cola first:


```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| label: fig-coke
#| fig-cap: "Map displaying the number of Coca-Cola plastics collected during [*Break Free From Plastic*](https://www.breakfreefromplastic.org/) cleanups by country."

world_plastics |> 
  
  # filter to keep only "The Coca-Cola Company" entries in the parent_company column
  filter(parent_company == "The Coca-Cola Company") |> 
  
  # then make a simple plot
  ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = world,
               aes(x = long, y = lat,    # plotting the map underneath the data
                   group = group),
               fill = "lightgray",
               color = "darkgray")+
  geom_polygon(aes(x = long, 
                   y = lat,              # plotting the number of plastics per country
                   group = group,
                   fill = grand_total))+
  scale_fill_continuous(palette = c("#37c6ed", "#2273b5", "#090f66"))   # change the colors of the fill to look pretty

```


Ok let's do it with the rest of the companies, log transform the plastic counts to help distinguish locations, and fix some of the other issues with @fig-coke above:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-align: center
#| label: fig-brands
#| fig-cap: "Maps displaying the number of Nestlé, PepsiCo, and Coca-Cola plastics collected during [*Break Free From Plastic*](https://www.breakfreefromplastic.org/) cleanups by country."

world_plastics |> 
  
  # first, filter to keep only the three companies of interest
  filter(parent_company == "The Coca-Cola Company"| 
         parent_company == "PepsiCo"|
         parent_company == "Nestlé") |> 
  
  # then, remove rows where grand_total = 0 as it appears to map 0s otherwise. Not sure if there's a better way to do this...
  filter_out(grand_total == "0") |> 
  
  # plot the new data
  ggplot() +
    geom_polygon(data = world,
                 aes(x = long, y = lat,         # base world map
                     group = group),
                 fill = "lightgray",
                 color = "darkgray")+
    geom_polygon(aes(x = long, 
                     y = lat,                   # plastic heatmap layer
                     group = group,
                     fill = grand_total))+  
    scale_fill_gradientn(transform = "log10",   # log transform the grand_total to better see smaller differences.
                         colors = c("#37c6ed", "#2273b5", "#090f66"),                 # make the colors pretty
                         guide = guide_colourbar(direction = "horizontal"))+     # make the legend horizontal
    facet_wrap(~parent_company, ncol=2)+       # facet wrap by company 
    theme_grey()+                              # grey theme
    theme(legend.position = c(0.8,0.2),        # make the legend sit in the empty space
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 23),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 15),
          axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),   # fix text sizes
          strip.text = element_text(size = 15),
          plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
          plot.tag.position = c(0.81,0.3))+  # move the tag label to be above the legend
    labs(fill = NULL,   # delete the legend title, using tag label instead for more flexibility in location
         title = "Amount of Nestlé, Pepsi, and Coke Plastic Pollution Collected per Country",
         subtitle = "Collected during Break Free From Plastic Cleanup Events",
         caption = "Gray = zero or N/A",
         x = "Longitude",
         y = "Latitude",
         tag = "log10 of Total Plastic")  # tag label is used instead of legend title

```


As we can see in @fig-brands, Nestlé and PepsiCo appear to have somewhat similar patterns of plastic distribution, while Coca-Cola appears in different regions.
